title: GrowWithHR POSH Wave 1 Governed Statutory Retrieval Catalogue

sourcePack.name: GrowWithHR POSH Wave 1 controlled statutory snapshot
sourcePack.notes: Curated source-grounded summaries from the controlled POSH Act, Rules and commencement records. Qualified legal review and exact controlled-file approval remain required.

sources.title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules, 2013

chunks.title: Employee definition
chunks.text: Section 2(f) defines employee broadly, including regular, temporary, ad hoc and daily-wage workers, persons engaged directly or through an agent or contractor, and co-workers, probationers, trainees and apprentices. Workforce and unit counts used by a deterministic rule must therefore follow the approved assessment boundary and must not be inferred from payroll headcount alone.

chunks.title: Constitution and unit coverage of the Internal Committee
chunks.text: Section 4(1) requires the employer to constitute an Internal Committee by an order in writing. Where offices or administrative units are located at different places or at divisional or sub-divisional level, committee coverage must be considered at those offices or administrative units. A company total cannot substitute for unit-level facts.

chunks.title: Internal Committee composition and tenure
chunks.text: Section 4(2) sets the core committee composition: a senior woman employee as Presiding Officer where available, at least two employee members with the specified commitment, experience or knowledge, and one external member from an appropriate non-governmental association or a person familiar with sexual-harassment issues. At least half of the members must be women. Section 4(3) limits nomination tenure to the period specified by the employer, not exceeding three years.

chunks.title: External-member fees or allowances
chunks.text: Rule 3 prescribes fees or allowances for the external member of the Internal Committee. It is supporting implementation material and does not replace the Section 4 composition conditions.

chunks.title: Local Committee route
chunks.text: Section 6 provides a Local Committee route for establishments where an Internal Committee has not been constituted because there are fewer than ten workers and for complaints against the employer. The product may record that the route exists, but must not decide an individual complaint or collect allegations.

chunks.title: Complaint, inquiry, confidentiality and appeal framework
chunks.text: Sections 9 to 18 establish the statutory complaint and redressal framework, including presentation of a complaint, conciliation limits, inquiry, interim measures, inquiry reports, action on recommendations, confidentiality and appeal. GrowWithHR evaluates only whether privacy-safe organisational controls are recorded; it does not assess any case, evidence, finding or outcome.

chunks.title: Prescribed complaint and inquiry procedure
chunks.text: Rules 6 to 12 provide prescribed procedural details supporting the statutory complaint and inquiry framework. The private-beta rule is intentionally control-only: it may check route, ownership, timeline, confidentiality and retention-control statuses, but it may not accept complaint narratives, identities, allegations, evidence or findings.

chunks.title: Employer duties: policy, display and programmes
chunks.text: Section 19 requires employers to provide a safe working environment, display the penal consequences of sexual harassment and the order constituting the Internal Committee, and organise workshops and awareness programmes for employees at regular intervals as well as orientation programmes for committee members. These duties support control reviews, not certification of content or quality.

chunks.title: Policy dissemination, orientation, awareness and capacity building
chunks.text: Rule 13 supplements Section 19 by addressing formulation and wide dissemination of an internal policy or declaration, orientation of committee members, employee awareness, capacity building and declaration of committee member names and contact details. GrowWithHR records only controlled categories and evidence references; personal contact details are not accepted into the explanation payload.

chunks.title: Annual report and employer disclosure duties
chunks.text: Section 21 requires the Internal Committee to prepare an annual report for each calendar year and submit it to the employer and District Officer. Section 22 requires the employer to include prescribed case information in its annual report or, where no such report is prepared, intimate the District Officer. The private-beta review records only year and control-presence indicators and never sends complaint counts or case details to a provider.

chunks.title: Prescribed annual-report content
chunks.text: Rule 14 prescribes annual-report content categories, including complaint statistics, pending matters, workshops or awareness programmes and action taken. GrowWithHR represents these only as present-or-not-present control indicators in this Wave 1 implementation, not as case-level data.

chunks.title: Commencement of the Act
chunks.text: The Central Government appointed 9 December 2013 as the date on which the provisions of the Act came into force. This commencement source supports effective-date metadata and does not itself determine whether an organisation has implemented a control.

limitations: Every decision is produced before retrieval by a versioned deterministic rule.
Retrieval is constrained to Source Register IDs and reason codes already present on the decision.
The chunks are source-grounded private-beta summaries and remain needs-legal-review.
No complaint narrative, identity, allegation, evidence, finding or case-level statistic is accepted for retrieval or provider explanation.
A retrieved chunk or language-model response cannot create a fact, change a status or certify compliance.
